questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

A beast of burden
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"A beast of burden" **best expresses the meaning *"An animal that carries luggage."*
 
• **"A beast of burden" **(भार वाहक पशु) refers to an animal that is used for carrying heavy loads or doing hard physical work.
 
• This phrase originates from the role of animals like horses, mules, oxen, camels, and elephants, which are traditionally used to carry heavy loads in various cultures.
 
• *"An animal that carries luggage"* (सामान उठाने वाला जानवर) is the best fit for the phrase because it directly describes what a beast of burden does.

Therefore, the **correct answer **is: *'An animal that carries luggage'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's go through each of the options:
 
 
• **"A liability"** (दायित्व) refers to something or someone that causes trouble or cost. This isn't a good fit for the phrase because a beast of burden is typically useful and helpful, not a source of trouble.
 
• **"A person who works hardly" **(जो व्यक्ति कठिनाई से काम करता है) isn't a perfect match for the phrase because it refers to people, not animals. However, sometimes the phrase "beast of burden" can be used metaphorically to describe a person who is carrying a heavy load, either physically or emotionally. The correct phrase should be "A person who works hard".
 
• **"A violent man"** (हिंसक आदमी) doesn't match the phrase at all. A beast of burden isn't necessarily violent – in fact, these animals are often docile and well-trained to handle their tasks.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

A piece of cake
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - **Something easy​.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the meaning of the given idiom:

 
 
• **A piece of cake **- something that is very easy to do.
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *The exam was a** piece of cake.***
 
 

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Let's look at the origin of the idiom:

 
 
• The idea of **cake **being “**easy**” originated in the 1870s when **cakes **were given out as **prizes **for winning competitions.
 
• In particular, there was a **tradition **in the US slavery states where slaves would circle a **cake **at a gathering.
 
• The most “**graceful**” pair would win the **cake** in the middle.
 
• From this, the term **“cakewalk”** and **“piece of cake” **came into being, both meaning that something was **easy to accomplish.**

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To breast the tape
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To breast the tape" **is an idiomatic expression originating from competitive running.
 
• In a race, **a tape is stretched **across the finish line.
 
• The first person to break this tape with their chest, or** "breast the tape," is the winner. **(दौड़ में जीतना)
 
• So, it essentially **means** "To win a race".

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'To win a race'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To shut someone’s mouth **- This phrase generally means to cause someone to stop speaking, often by making them feel guilty or embarrassed. It does not have a similar meaning to "To breast the tape". (किसी का मूंह बंद करना).
 
• **To create problems** - This phrase means to cause difficulties or obstacles. (समस्याएँ पैदा करना).
 
• **To bring joy** - This phrase means to make someone feel happy or satisfied. Although winning a race can bring joy, this phrase is not specifically equivalent to "To breast the tape".(खुशी लाना).

• It is a **"reference to any process by which cataclysmic failure (a broken back) is achieved by a seemingly inconsequential addition, a single straw."**

Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

The plum tree in our garden __is cover in__ blossoms, as are the trees outside my office window.
questions.solution:

• The phrase** "is cover in" **is grammatically incorrect because "cover" is not in the correct form.
 
• The correct phrase should be **"is covered in,**" which is the past participle form of "cover" used in passive voice structures.
 
• The corrected sentence should read "The plum tree in our garden is covered in blossoms, as are the trees outside my office window."

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *The plum tree in our garden is covered in blossoms, as are the trees outside my office window.*

• Option 3, "No substitution required," is incorrect because the original phrase "is cover in" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Option 4, "is covering at," is incorrect because it uses the wrong verb form and preposition.
 
• Using the correct verb and preposition ensures the sentence is grammatically and contextually accurate.

Give cold shoulder

options.text: Start doing something before the appropriate time

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Ignore, avoid or be unfriendly towards someone**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is **4) Ignore, avoid or be unfriendly towards someone**.
 
• The idiom **"give cold shoulder" **means **to intentionally ignore, avoid, or be unfriendly towards someone.** It is an expression used to describe a behavior where someone is deliberately disregarded or treated with indifference.(किसी के प्रति जानबूझकर उपेक्षा करना, बचना या अमित्र होना। यह एक ऐसे व्यवहार का वर्णन करने के लिए उपयोग की जाने वाली अभिव्यक्ति है जहां किसी को जानबूझकर अवहेलना या उदासीनता से व्यवहार किया जाता है।)
 
 
• Example: "Sarah tried to talk to her colleague about an important matter, but he **gave her the cold shoulder** and walked away without acknowledging her."
 
• In this example, the colleague intentionally ignores Sarah and shows unfriendliness by walking away without acknowledging her attempt to engage in a conversation.(इस उदाहरण में, सहकर्मी जानबूझकर सारा की उपेक्षा करता है और बातचीत में शामिल होने के उसके प्रयास को स्वीकार किए बिना दूर जाकर मित्रता दिखाता है।)
 
 
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate meaning of the idiom **"give cold shoulder"** is to ignore, avoid, or be unfriendly towards someone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **To shoot at **(गोली चलाना): To fire a gun at someone or something.

 
 
• **Example:** The soldier was ordered to shoot at the target.
 
 
 
• **To become a rebel **(विद्रोही बनना): To oppose or defy authority or tradition.
 
 
• **Example: **He decided to become a rebel and fight against the unjust system.
 
 
 
• **To become unfaithful to** (अवफादार होना): To stop being loyal or faithful.
 
 
• **Example:** She feared he would become unfaithful to her.
